plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms rise on sturdy stems in rows of saturated color, and fields of them look like painted stripes across the flat Dutch landscape. In late April the late-season varieties are at their peak, long after the first early tulips have faded.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late spring, with peak bloom in mid to late April in the Netherlands
plants.location: Lisse and the bulb-growing region of the Netherlands
plants.funFact: In the 1630s tulip bulbs were so prized in the Dutch Republic that single bulbs sold for more than the price of a canal house, in a speculative frenzy now known as tulip mania.

plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant clusters of blossom hang from twisting vines, making curtains and tunnels of lavender. Bees crowd the racemes, and the scent drifts well beyond the garden gate.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid April to mid May, with peak bloom around late April to early May
plants.location: Japan, including the wisteria gardens of Honshu and Kyushu
plants.funFact: Japanese wisteria twines clockwise, while its Chinese relative twines counterclockwise. Old vines can live for centuries and grow to enormous size.

plants.name: Cyclamen persicum
plants.description: Swept-back petals look like tiny butterflies hovering above heart-shaped leaves marbled in silver. In the rocky Mediterranean hillsides of the eastern Mediterranean, this wild ancestor of the florist's cyclamen blooms in dappled shade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, often lingering into April at higher elevations
plants.location: Eastern Mediterranean, including Israel, Lebanon, Turkey and Cyprus
plants.funFact: After flowering, the stem coils like a spring and pulls the seed capsule down toward the soil, which helps plant the seeds close to the parent.
